subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Data Interpretation — Student Performance Table (W10 B2)

questions.stem:
The table below shows marks scored (out of 100) by 5 students across 5 subjects:

Student  | Science | Maths | English | History | Geography | Total
Ananya   |   85    |  72   |   68    |   75    |    80     | 380
Bikram   |   70    |  88   |   75    |   65    |    72     | 370
Chitra   |   90    |  65   |   82    |   70    |    78     | 385
Dhruv    |   60    |  92   |   55    |   80    |    65     | 352
Esha     |   75    |  78   |   70    |   85    |    82     | 390

Who scored the highest total marks?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Totals: Ananya=380, Bikram=370, Chitra=385, Dhruv=352, Esha=390. Esha has the highest total (390). Trap: Chitra (385) is second highest — students who confuse Chitra and Esha's totals pick C.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table (same as Q1), in which subject did all five students together score the lowest combined marks?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Column totals: Science=380, Maths=395, English=350, History=375, Geography=377. English has the lowest combined total (350). Trap: Dhruv's 55 in English is the lowest individual score, correctly flagging English as the weakest subject collectively.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, what is Ananya's average score across all five subjects?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Ananya's total = 85+72+68+75+80 = 380. Average = 380/5 = 76. Trap: 74 uses total 370 (Bikram's total); 78 divides by 4 instead of 5.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, who scored the highest marks in Science?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Science scores: Ananya=85, Bikram=70, Chitra=90, Dhruv=60, Esha=75. Chitra has the highest Science score (90). Trap: Ananya (85) is second — students confuse the highest scorer with the second highest.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, by how many marks does Chitra's total exceed Dhruv's total?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Chitra = 385; Dhruv = 352. Difference = 385−352 = 33. Trap: 30 = 385−355 (misreads Dhruv's total); 25 = 385−360 (wrong subtraction).

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, what is the difference between the highest and lowest subject column totals?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Column totals: Science=380, Maths=395, English=350, History=375, Geography=377. Highest = Maths (395), Lowest = English (350). Difference = 395−350 = 45. Trap: 40 uses Geography (377) as lowest; 35 uses History (375) as highest.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, what percentage of Maths column total did Bikram score? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Bikram's Maths = 88. Maths column total = 395. Percentage = (88/395)×100 = 22.28% ≈ 22.3%. Trap: 20.5% = 88/430 (wrong total); 23.5% = 92/395 (Dhruv's Maths score, not Bikram's).

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, if Dhruv's Science score increases by 20 marks and his English score decreases by 8 marks, what is his new total?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Dhruv's current total = 352. Science increases by 20 and English decreases by 8: net change = +20−8 = +12. New total = 352+12 = 364. Trap: 360 = 352+8 (uses only the English change); 368 = 352+16 (adds both changes as positive).

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, what is the ratio of Esha's History score to Ananya's History score?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Esha's History = 85. Ananya's History = 75. Ratio = 85:75 = 17:15 (divide both by 5). Trap: 15:17 reverses the ratio (Ananya:Esha instead of Esha:Ananya); 16:15 misreads one score.

questions.stem: Using the student performance table, marks are out of 100 per subject (total maximum = 500). Esha needs at least 80% to qualify for a scholarship. Does she qualify?

options.option_text: No — she scores 78%, which is below 80%
No — she scores 75%, which is below 80%

questions.explanation: C is correct. Esha's total = 390 out of 500. Percentage = 390/500×100 = 78%. Scholarship threshold = 80% of 500 = 400. Esha scores 390 < 400, so she does NOT qualify. Her percentage (78%) falls 2% short. Trap: 80% of 390 ≠ 80% of 500 — some students compute 80% incorrectly using her own score as denominator.
